NS-4 makes the $6.61 statutorily chargeable once the rider cancels past 3 minutes and Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a driver running late, so the only remedy available on these facts is the NS-7 manual fee-waiver channel, which the rider is invoking within time.
The amount in dispute is exactly $6.61, computed from the cancellation fee on the fare record (no surge multiplier 1.0× applies), and under NS-7 it is issuable as a Ryde voucher rather than cash.
The rider is a 2.3-year account with rating 4.5 and zero disputes in 90 days, while the driver carries 1 dispute in 90 days, so waiving the fee is not rewarding abusive cancellation behaviour.

weaknesses: The decisive fact against us is F2: the cancellation was at 21:33:20, 20 seconds past the 3-minute boundary, which under NS-4 makes the $6.61 chargeable and bars the automatic free-cancellation route; C1 concedes this.

The policy contains no rider-side remedy for a driver who is late or never arrives: NS-8 (Grab/Gojek 'driver past ETA = free cancellation') is marked 不可引用, so it cannot be cited to defeat the fee, and F8's 'tomorrow' five-minute claim is a chat statement that the GPS record F1 contradicts.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The case enters the cancellation branch through NS-0: the cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so only NS-4/NS-5 can apply, and the trip was an immediate (non-advanced) RydeX booking, leaving NS-4. On the timing element, the booking was accepted at 21:30:00 and cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s (200 s) after matching [F2], which is past the 3-minute mark; the execution trace confirms NS-4 "rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching" = ✓ and the only allowed outcome is no_action. NS-4's first sentence makes cancellations within 3 minutes free and cancellations beyond it chargeable, so the $6.61 recorded on the fare line [F5] is a valid charge; with no surge multiplier [F6] the disputed amount is exactly the fee on record, 6.61 SGD, with nothing to recompute (no meter, no off-route km, non-metered RydeX fare) [F5][F6][RD-2].

The rider's strongest argument is that the driver was still 2501 m away at 21:31:20 and never came within 200 m [F1], with no arrival recorded [F3] and no "I'm Here" tap [F4], so the fee is unfair. Those facts are accepted as true — the system records beat the driver's chat claim of "About 5 min, traffic" [F8] and his statement that he was on his way [F9] — but they do not defeat the charge. Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right based on driver lateness or a missed ETA; the ETA-based rules of other platforms are expressly informative and non-citable (NS-8), and the policy itself directs the rider in NS-4 to the manual remedy rather than to an automatic waiver. The driver's traffic excuse is also weak: the only congestion record is a band 3 (20–29 km/h) reading on Jalan Buroh [F10] with no incident near the route [F11] in fair weather [F12], and band 3 alone falls short of the severe-congestion corroboration required by RD-4(b) — but that weakness concerns route justification, not the rider-side cancellation branch, and here the driver asserted no no-show claim [F3][F4].

NS-1 and NS-2 therefore never engage: they exist only where the driver cancels while claiming a rider no-show under NS-0, and here the rider cancelled, and the driver never pressed "I'm Here" nor had any arrival recorded [F3][F4]. Because NS-1's conditions were never triggered, the NS-2 full-refund branch and its fraud flag are unavailable, and no waiting fee was ever asserted (only the $6.61 cancellation fee appears) [F4][F5]. Profile facts cannot decide the case: the rider's clean 2.3-year record [F13] and the driver's 1081 trips with 0 upheld disputes [F14] are both set aside as non-decisive, and in any event RD-6 is not engaged since there is no upheld route violation and no refundable amount in this no-show dispute.

The fee remains a charge the rider can try to have waived at Ryde's discretion within 30 days and paid as a voucher (NS-7), but that is a discretionary human channel, not a rule entitling the rider to a refund; the policy gives no clause that converts a validly charged post-3-minute cancellation fee into a refund. The complaint therefore does not succeed and the charge stands.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider cancellation fee; the rider may still file a discretionary voucher request via RydeHELP within 30 days (NS-7), but no automatic refund is ordered.

certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 200 s after acceptance (F2)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled a live (non-advanced) RydeX booking 3 min 20 s after matching at 21:30:00, i.e. after the 3-minute mark, so the branch is NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider) → NS-4, and the $6.61 fee is chargeable.
The driver never entered the pickup area: his closest approach was 2501 m at 21:31:20 and he never came within 200 m, which explains why no arrival was ever recorded (driver_arrived_at is null).

The driver never pressed 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the arrival/waiting condition required for the rider to bear a no-show fee was never established, and the rider's cancellation cannot be a 'no show' at all.

There is no traffic excuse: the only congestion record is JALAN BUROH (category 3) at band 3 (20–29 km/h) and no traffic incidents were recorded anywhere near the route during the trip window, in fair weather with 0.0 mm rain — consistent with the driver being 2.5 km away 80 seconds after he told the rider 'About 5 min, traffic'.

NS-4 makes the $6.61 statutorily chargeable once the rider cancels past 3 minutes and Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a driver running late, so the only remedy available on these facts is the NS-7 manual fee-waiver channel, which the rider is invoking within time.
The amount in dispute is exactly $6.61, computed from the cancellation fee on the fare record (no surge multiplier 1.0× applies), and under NS-7 it is issuable as a Ryde voucher rather than cash.
The rider is a 2.3-year account with rating 4.5 and zero disputes in 90 days, while the driver carries 1 dispute in 90 days, so waiving the fee is not rewarding abusive cancellation behaviour.

weaknesses: The decisive fact against us is F2: the cancellation was at 21:33:20, 20 seconds past the 3-minute boundary, which under NS-4 makes the $6.61 chargeable and bars the automatic free-cancellation route; C1 concedes this.

The policy contains no rider-side remedy for a driver who is late or never arrives: NS-8 (Grab/Gojek 'driver past ETA = free cancellation') is marked 不可引用, so it cannot be cited to defeat the fee, and F8's 'tomorrow' five-minute claim is a chat statement that the GPS record F1 contradicts.

The driver's statement F9 ('I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is not rebutted by any intent evidence — GPS only shows he was 2501 m away (F1), which is consistent with genuinely being en route, just too far.

Our 'no-show' framing is weak: because the driver cancelled nothing and never claimed a no-show (F3, F4), NS-1/NS-2 never really engage and neither does the fraud flag in NS-2, so we cannot obtain a refund_full under the no-show branch — the best available route is NS-7 discretionary waiver.
The rider never contacted the driver after 21:31 nor used the app before cancelling (F7, F8), which the fare side can use to argue the rider chose to cancel rather than wait out the driver's ETA.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled the RydeX trip 3 min 20 s after acceptance, i.e. outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable under NS-4 and no refund is owed to the rider.
NS-1 does not apply here because the cancellation was made by the rider, not by the driver claiming a no-show, so the NS-2 refund branch triggered by a failed NS-1 is not engaged.

The rider's own account confirms she chose to cancel after being told the driver was about 5 minutes away; the driver was actively en route and never had the chance to arrive before the rider cancelled, so no waiting-fee or no-show obligation of the driver was breached.

Ryde's rules do not provide a free cancellation merely because the driver has not yet arrived; the driver did not tap "I'm Here" or trigger any waiting fee, so the only fee at issue is the rider-side cancellation fee that NS-4 permits.
The driver's record supports good faith rather than fee abuse: 1081 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes of any kind, consistent with the driver simply being en route when the rider cancelled.

weaknesses: The GPS record shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 2501 m at 21:31:20 and he never came within 200 m (F1), and the platform never recorded arrival (F3) — the rider will use this to argue the driver was unreasonably far after 3 minutes and that charging $6.61 is unfair.

The driver himself told the rider 'About 5 min, traffic' at 21:31 (F8), while the only traffic data shows merely band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Jalan Buroh — not a band 1–2 severe-congestion record — and no incidents on the route (F10, F11), so the 'traffic' excuse is weakly corroborated.

Although NS-4 makes the fee chargeable on timing alone and Ryde publishes no ETA-based free-cancellation rule, the rider's fairness argument (F2, F1) may still persuade a human reviewer under NS-7 discretion.

points.response: Conceded on liability: the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, 3 min 20 s after matching (F2), so NS-4 makes the $6.61 chargeable on timing alone and my C1 already said so — but that is the end of the driver's case, not the end of the dispute, because NS-4's own text leaves the rider the NS-7 manual fee-waiver channel and the fee remains chargeable only as a fee, not as an entitlement the driver may defend on false grounds.

D2 is correct as far as it goes and I never claimed otherwise: NS-1/NS-2 do not engage, and I do not ask for the NS-2 fraud flag — but the rider relies on NS-1 only to show the negative fact that the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' (F4) and no arrival was ever recorded (F3), which rebuts any suggestion the rider was a no-show who was 'found' waiting.

D3 asks the judge to accept the driver's chat claims – F8 'About 5 min, traffic' and F9 'I was on my way' – over the system record, and the record shows the driver was still 2501 m from the pickup 80 seconds after that promise and never came within 200 m at any point (F1); under the system-record-wins rule a bare statement loses to F1, and 'actively en route' does not rebut that the driver was 2.5 km away when the rider cancelled.

D4 proves only that $6.61 was lawfully debited under NS-4, not that it should be retained after review — NS-7 exists precisely for this case and is the provision the driver's brief omits entirely, and the driver also asserts no waiting fee or arrival fee was triggered (F3, F4), so the entire $6.61 represents a charge for a ride never begun from a driver who never got near the rider.

D5 proves nothing about this trip: 1081 trips with 0 upheld disputes (F14) is a profile fact that under the rules can never decide a finding, and it cuts weakly against the driver anyway since F1 shows he was 2.5 km from the pickup rather than any evidence that he was close when the rider gave up.

Unchanged and now reinforced: NS-4 caps the rider's case at the NS-7 discretionary waiver for the $6.61 (F2, F5), and the rider is within the 30-day window, so the right outcome is refund_full by voucher rather than the driver's no_action.

Accepted, and it is the rider's own concession: the cancellation at 21:33:20 was 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark (F2), so NS-4 makes the $6.61 chargeable and the automatic free-cancellation route is closed.

We agree NS-4 governs; but C5's own logic means no clause of this policy defeats the fee, and NS-7 is a deadline-and-form rule for a human fee-waiver request, not a ground for this tribunal to order a refund — nothing in NS-7 makes an otherwise chargeable fee refundable.

The 2501 m closest approach and the null arrival record (F1, F3) show only that the driver had not yet reached the pickup when the rider jumped ship at 3 min 20 s; they prove no breach, because the rider-side branch NS-4 turns on the cancellation timing, not on driver proximity (F2).

The absence of an 'I'm Here' tap (F4) is a point in the driver's favour: it means no no-show claim and no waiting fee was ever asserted against the rider, so the only money on the table is the statutory rider cancellation fee she elected to incur (F2, F5).

The traffic record is not part of the driver's defence and we do not rely on it: the driver's case is that he was genuinely en route and was told about 5 minutes (F8), and under NS-4 the state of the road does not affect whether a post-3-minute rider cancellation is chargeable (F2).
Agreed on the arithmetic — $6.61 with no surge (F5, F6) — but that amount is precisely what NS-4 authorises Ryde to keep, and NS-7 does not convert a valid charge into a refund.

Profile facts cannot decide this case, and in any event the driver's 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F14) means no adverse finding against him, while his 1081 trips in 90 days support a driver who was working the trip rather than gaming a fee.
